chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from more than one of our companions, from Abi 'Abdillah عليه السلام, who said:

There is no wudu (ablution) due for madhy arising from desire, nor from arousal, nor from kissing, nor from touching the private part, nor from lying together; and neither the garment nor the body is washed because of it.

key_terms.وُضُوءٌ: wudu (ablution), which the hadith negates as obligatory here
key_terms.ٱلثَّوْبُ: the garment, which does not need washing because of it
key_terms.ٱلشَّهْوَةِ: sexual desire as one cause associated with the emission
key_terms.ٱلْإِنْعَاظِ: arousal or erection mentioned among the causes
key_terms.ٱلْقُبْلَةِ: kissing, cited as one circumstance in which the emission may occur
key_terms.ٱلْمَذْيِ: pre-seminal fluid mentioned as the subject of the ruling
key_terms.ٱلْمُضَاجَعَةِ: lying together or sharing a bed

ai.seo_question: Does madhy require wudu (ablution) or washing the body and clothes in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on madhy, stating that its emission in the mentioned circumstances does not require wudu (ablution). It also states that it does not necessitate washing the clothing or the body, indicating that it is not treated here as a substance requiring ritual cleansing in these cases.
